Rashi on Zevachim 3b:10:1.hebrew: חטאת ששחטה לשם חטאת - היינו חטאת חלב ששחטה לשם חטאת דם. והא מילתא מבוארת לקמן בפירקין (זבחים דף ז.):
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:10:1.english: A sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering - That is, a sin offering [brought for transgressing the prohibition of] forbidden fat, which one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering [brought for a transgression involving] blood. And this matter [is explained] later in this chapter (Zevachim 7a).

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:11:1.hebrew: והאמר רב - בשינוי בעלים: חטאת ראובן ששחטה להתכפר בה שמעון, אם שמעון מחוייב חטאת (הוה) — פסולה; אבל אם מחוייב עולה ולא חטאת — כשרה. אלמא, לאו מיניה לאו מחריב ביה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:11:1.english: But doesn't Rav say - [This refers to] a change of owner: [If] Reuven's sin offering was slaughtered in order to atone for Shimon, if Shimon is obligated to bring a sin offering, it is unfit; but if he is obligated to bring a burnt offering and not a sin offering, it is fit. Apparently, [an intention] that is not of its type does not ruin it.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:12:1.hebrew: התם - שינוי קודש נפקא לן [לפסולא מושחט] אותה לחטאת, שתהא שחיטה לשם חטאת. וכאן הרי חטאת לשם חטאת נשחטה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:12:1.english: There - We derive [the disqualification of] a change of sanctity [i.e., slaughtering an offering for the sake of a different type of offering] from [the verse] “and slaughter it for a sin offering,” meaning that the slaughter must be for the sake of a sin offering. But here, behold, a sin offering was slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:13:1.hebrew: הכא - בשינוי בעלים פסולה נפקא לן מעליו ולא על חבירו. והילכך, חבירו דומיא דידיה — דבר מיניה הוא דמחריב ביה לבטולי שמיה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:13:1.english: Here - That a [sin offering slaughtered] with a change of owner is invalid, we derive from "for him" and not for his fellow. And therefore, "his fellow" must be similar to him: it is something of its own kind that one undermines through it, to nullify its name.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:17:1.hebrew: ארבעה תוכו כתיבי - כיצד? "תוכו" תרי זימני, ודרוש "תוך" ודרוש "תוכו", דהוה מצי למיכתב "אל תוך", וכתיב "תוכו" למיעוטא. וכן בחבירו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:17:1.english: "Tokho" is written four [times] - How so? "Tokho" appears twice, and one expounds [it as] "tokh" and expounds [it as] "tokho", since [the verse] could have written "el tokh" (into the interior), yet it wrote "tokho" (its interior) to exclude [something]. And likewise with its counterpart [the second instance]:

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:18:1.hebrew: חד לגופיה - שיטמא כלי חרס [אוכלין] מאוירן:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:18:1.english: One for its own matter - That [an earthenware vessel] imparts impurity to [foods] from its airspace.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:18:2.hebrew: וחד לג"ש - ללמוד שיטמא שרץ את הכלי, ואע"פ שלא נגע בו כו', כדיליף ליה בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף כד:): נאמר "תוכו" ליטמא, ונאמר "תוכו" לטמא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:18:2.english: And one for a verbal analogy - [To teach] that a creeping creature renders the vessel impure, even though it did not touch [it], etc., as [the Gemara] derives it in the chapter Hakol Shochatin (Chullin 24b): It says "its interior" regarding becoming impure, and it says "its interior" regarding rendering impure.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:19:1.hebrew: ולא תוכו של אחר - למעוטי כלי שטף מטומאת אויר, אא"כ נגע:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:19:1.english: And not the interior of another - This serves to exclude a vessel [that is purified by] rinsing from impurity [transmitted through] airspace, unless [the source of impurity] touched it.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:19:2.hebrew: וחד תוכו ולא תוך תוכו - כדפרישית לעיל. וע"כ עיקר קרא לכלי שטף אתא, דאי למעוטי כלי חרס שבתוך התנור, ופיו למעלה מפי התנור, שיציל על האוכלין שבתוכו — למה לי וי"ו יתירא למעוטי? לכתוב "כל אשר [בתוך] יטמא"! ומהיכא תיתי לטמויי אוכלים שבפנימי? הא לאו תוכו נינהו! אלא ללמד על כלי שטף שאף הוא יציל, דלא תימא דלאו מיניה, לאו מחריב ביה. הילכך גזירת הכתוב היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:19:2.english: And one [teaches] its interior but not the interior of its interior - As I explained above. And necessarily, the main purpose of the verse comes for a rinsed vessel; for if it were to exclude an earthenware vessel that is inside the oven, whose mouth is above the mouth of the oven, so that it protects the food inside it — why do I need the extra *vav* to exclude? Let it write, "all that is [in it] shall be impure"! And from where would we have reason to render impure the food in the inner vessel? Surely it is not its interior! Rather, [the extra *vav* comes] to teach about a rinsed vessel, that it too protects, so that you should not say that since it is not of its kind, it does not [serve to] destroy through it. Therefore, it is a decree of the verse.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:1.hebrew: אם הציל - אם המחיצה הצילה במת החמור באהל המת, שהמחיצה מפסקת, וכלים שמעבר השני טהורין, דכתיב (במדבר יט) כל אשר באהל יטמא, והני לאו בההוא אהל נינהו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:1.english: If it protects - If a partition protects against the severe impurity of a corpse in the tent of the dead — since the partition divides, and the vessels on the other side are pure, as it is written (Numbers 19:14), "all that is in the tent shall be impure," and these are not in that same tent:

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:2.hebrew: שכן חולקין - דרך בני אדם לחלוק אוהלין במחיצה. הלכך, אהל אחרינא הוא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:2.english: For they are divided - It is the way of people to divide tents with a partition. Therefore, it is a different tent.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:3.hebrew: תציל בכלי חרס - [בתמיה, שאין חולקין כלי חרס] במחיצות, הלכך תוכו קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:1:3.english: Should it protect in an earthenware vessel - [This is stated] incredulously, since partitions do not divide an earthenware vessel; therefore, we apply to it the term "its interior."

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:2:2.hebrew: אלא לר' אליעזר מאי איכא למימר - לימא שהדבר תלוי במחלוקת דרב תנאי היא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:2:2.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer, what can be said? - Let us say that it is [a matter of] a dispute among Tannaim.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:3:1.hebrew: ר' אליעזר קל וחומר קאמר - לעולם בעלמא ר' אליעזר כרב סבירא ליה, כגון חולין וקדשים. אבל לענין מחיצה, מקל וחומר יליף: כיון דבמת החמור מצלא, קל וחומר לכלי חרס הקל, שהשרץ קל מן המת:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:3:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer states an a fortiori argument - In general, Rabbi Eliezer holds like Rav, for example [regarding] non-sacred items and sacred items. But with regard to a partition, he derives it from an a fortiori argument: Since [a partition] protects against [impurity from] a corpse, which is more severe, then certainly [it protects] an earthenware vessel, which is lighter, as [the impurity of] a creeping creature is lighter than that of a corpse.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:5:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: אלא טעמא דרב כ<abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> אלעזר. "ולא יחללו את קדשי" — הכי דריש ליה: אין דבר אחר מחלל את קדשי בני ישראל, וגזירת הכתוב היא. ופרכינן: אלמא לר' אלעזר, דבעית לאוקמה לדרב אליביה, אתא קרא דלא יחללו ואפקיה מ<abbr title="קל וחומר">ק"ו</abbr> דהוה לן למידרש "קדשים מחללין קדשים" כו':
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:5:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "Rather, the reasoning of Rav is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar." "And they shall not desecrate the sacred items of" — this is how he expounds it: Nothing else desecrates the sacred items of the children of Israel, and this is a decree of the verse. And we challenge: Evidently, according to Rabbi Elazar — according to whose view you wished to establish [the position of] Rav — the verse "they shall not desecrate" came and removed it from [the conclusion of] an a fortiori argument, [since otherwise] we would have had to derive that "sacred items desecrate sacred items," etc.:

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:6:1.hebrew: ה"נ ליתי תוכו - קרא יתירא דדרשינן לקמן "תוכו" ולא תוך תוכו (וקאמרת מקרא למידק, למידרש תוכו ולא תוך תוכו), וקאמרת מסברא דלא ממעט אלא תוך כלי אחר, אבל מחיצה דלאו בת מיניה לית ליה לאיחרוביה אי לאו משום קל וחומר. ואמאי אמרת קל וחומר? ליתי "תוכו" וליפקיה! דמדמעט תוך תוכו, מכלל דתוכו לעולם טמא. דאי מחיצה (בעלמא) מצלא, למה לי קרא למעוטי תוך תוכו? השתא תוכו מציל, תוך תוכו מבעיא? והאי שבעבר המחיצה תוכו הוא לרב, דהאמרת דלאו מיניה לא מחריב ביה. ומשיב: אמר לך ר' אלעזר: האי "תוכו" דאתי למעוטי תוך תוכו, ובעית למידק מיניה מחיצה לא מצלא:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:6:1.english: Here too, let "its interior" come - The superfluous verse, from which we derive below "its interior," but not the interior of its interior (and you say that the verse is to be expounded as teaching "its interior" and not the interior of its interior); and you say that, based on logic, it excludes only the interior of another vessel, but a partition, which is not of the same kind, would not render it [the food] impure, were it not for the *a fortiori* inference. So why did you say [that it is derived from] an *a fortiori* inference? Let "its interior" come and rule it out! For since it excludes the interior of its interior, it follows that its interior is always impure. For if a partition [in general] protects, why do I need a verse to exclude the interior of its interior? Now that "its interior" protects, is there any question about the interior of its interior? And this [item] that is beyond the partition is "its interior" according to Rav, who said that [a partition] that is not of its own kind does not make it impure. [The Gemara answers:] Rabbi Eliezer would say to you: This "its interior," which comes to exclude the interior of its interior, [is the reason for the exclusion], and you wish to infer from it that a partition does not protect?

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:7:1.hebrew: מיבעי ליה לאוכלין שגיבלן - וחיפן בטיט סביב, שאין השרץ יכול ליגע בהן, והכניסן לאויר התנור. והני הוא דאיתרבו לטומאה מדרשא. דלא תוך תוכו הוא, כדקאמרת: תוך תוכו הוא דמציל, אבל הקפת טיט לא מיחרבא ביה לבטולי שם תוכו, דלאו מיניה כה"ג לא מחריב ביה. דס"ד אמינא: הואיל וא"א להם ליטמא במגע שרץ, לא נטמאו נמי מתורת אויר כלי חרס. קמ"ל מיעוטא דלא תוך תוכו הוא (דאמר) דלא מטמא, אבל הני מיטמו. ומיהו מחיצה, אע"ג דלאו מיניה הוא, אתא ק"ו ורבייה לאיחרובי ביה:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:7:1.english: It is necessary for food that one kneaded - and plastered it with clay all around, so that the creeping animal cannot touch it, and put it into the airspace of the oven. And these are what was included for impurity by the exegesis, for it is not "its interior's interior," as you said: it is "its interior" that saves. But an enclosure of clay does not nullify its status as "interior," since [the clay] is not made of it [the oven]; a [barrier] of this kind does not nullify it. For it might have entered your mind to say: since they cannot become impure by the touch of a creeping animal, they also would not become impure through the law of the airspace of an earthenware vessel. [The verse] teaches us, through the exclusion of "it is not its interior's interior," that [the oven] does not become impure [when the food is separated], but these [foods] do become impure. Nevertheless, as for a partition, even though it is not made of it [the oven], a kal vachomer came and included it as nullifying [the status of interior].

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:8:1.hebrew: ורבנן הני - אוכלין לא צריכי קרא. הך וי"ו יתירא דדריש לקמן למעוטי תוך תוכו, ואיתרבו הנך אוכלין [דלאו] מיניה נינהו, לא איצטריך קרא לרבויינהו, דהני מתוך נפקי, דהא בתוך נינהו, ומהיכא תיתי לך לטהרינהו? והא דקאמר ״הואיל ובנגיעה לא מטמאו״, לאו איריא היא לטהרינהו מדין אויר:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:8:1.english: And the Rabbis, these - foodstuffs do not need a verse. That extra letter vav, which is expounded below to exclude the "inside of its inside," and these [foodstuffs] that are not of it (the vessel itself) were included — a verse was not needed to include them, for these emerge from the inside, since they are indeed inside, and from where would it occur to you to declare them pure? And as for what [the Gemara] said, "Since they do not become impure through contact," that is not a proper reason to declare them pure from the law of airspace.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:9:1.english: Deviation of the offering - [Slaughtering] a sin-offering for the sake of a burnt-offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 3b:9:2.hebrew: שינוי בעלים - חטאת ראובן ששחטה לשם שמעון להתכפר בה שמעון, דקיימא לן [לקמן] דפסולה, דכתיב: לכפר עליו ולא על חבירו:
Rashi on Zevachim 3b:9:2.english: Change of owner - For example: Reuven's sin offering that Reuven slaughtered for the sake of Shimon, for Shimon to achieve atonement through it. For we hold (later on) that it is disqualified, as it is written: “to atone for him” and not for his fellow.

Steinsaltz comment #3 on Zevachim 3a:8.english: That something which is not of its type at all, such as ordinary (non-sacred) items regarding sacred items, is not considered something that can be applied to nullify the name of the offering from it (Rashi).

Steinsaltz on Zevachim 3a:11.english: And Rava raised another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered it for the sake of ordinary meat it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type disqualifies it, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type does not disqualify it.

Tosafot on Zevachim 3b:4:1.hebrew: הכא נמי נימא קל וחומר קדשים מחללין קדשים כו' - יש תימה, דעד השתא אסיקנא איפכא מתוך הסברא, דאדרבה בשביל שהם קדשים ומינה לכך מחריב בה, אבל חולין דלאו בר מינה לא מחריב. ונראה לפרש דעביד קל וחומר, משום דמה קדשים שאין מחללין, כגון בשוחט חטאת סתם וכסבור שהיא עולה דכשירה, ואפ"ה מחללין קדשים בשוחט לשם עולה; חולין שמחללין, כגון בכסבור שהן חולין, דאמר בסוף בית שמאי (לקמן זבחים דף מו:) משום חולין פסולה, לא כל שכן שמחללין קדשים בשוחטן לשם חולין:
Tosafot on Zevachim 3b:4:1.english: "Here too, let us say an a fortiori inference: sacrificial animals desecrate sacrificial animals," etc. - There is a difficulty, for until now we concluded the opposite from logic: on the contrary, because they are sacrificial animals and of the same kind, [the slaughter for another sacrifice] destroys it, but non-sacred animals, which are not of the same kind, do not destroy. And it appears to explain that [the Gemara] makes an a fortiori inference because: if sacrificial animals, which do not [always] desecrate — for example, one who slaughters a sin offering without specification and thinks it is a burnt offering, in which case it is valid — nevertheless desecrate sacrificial animals when one slaughters for the sake of a burnt offering; then non-sacred animals, which do desecrate — for example, when one thinks they are non-sacred, as it says at the end of [the chapter] Beit Shammai (below, Zevachim 46b), "for the sake of non-sacred [meat] it is invalid" — all the more so do they desecrate sacrificial animals when one slaughters them for the sake of non-sacred [meat].

Tosafot on Zevachim 3b:5:1.hebrew: לא יחללו את קדשי בני ישראל - אע"ג דהאי קרא כתיב בטבל ובתרומה, כדמוכח לקמן (זבחים דף יא:) בגמרא דשמעון אחי עזריה, מכל מקום דריש רב מקרא זה דילמא "קדשי" מיותר קדריש, דהוה מצי למיכתב "ולא יחללו את אשר ירימו":
Tosafot on Zevachim 3b:5:1.english: "And they shall not desecrate the sacred items of the children of Israel" - Even though this verse is written regarding tevel and terumah, as is proven below (Zevachim 11b) in the Gemara of Shimon the brother of Azaria, [nevertheless Rav derives a teaching from it, since] perhaps he expounds the word "sacred items" as superfluous, for [the verse] could have written, "And they shall not desecrate that which they set apart":

Zevachim 3a:11.english: Ravina continued to inform Rav Pappa of Rava’s statements: Rava further raises another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered the animal for the sake of ordinary meat, it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type, i.e., for the sake of another offering, disqualifies the offering, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type, i.e., for the sake of ordinary meat, is disregarded and does not disqualify the offering.
